Company achieves $1.22 million in quarterly revenue and a 55% net profit margin as additional investment offerings are underway on its real-world asset marketplace.

Las Vegas, Nevada, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Primior Holdings Inc. (OTCMKT: PTKN) today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, highlighted by significant year-over-year profitability growth, improved operating margins, and continued expansion of the GAIA Marketplace ecosystem.

The Company more than doubled its quarterly net income compared to the same period last year, reflecting improved operational efficiency while continuing to advance its strategy of integrating real estate, private markets, and asset tokenization through a unified digital investment platform.

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights (Unaudited)

  • Gross margin: 74.0%, compared to 69.3% in Q3 2025
  • Operating income: $674,141, +89.3% YoY
  • Net income: $674,141, +101.6% YoY
  • Net profit margin: 55.0%, compared to 30.4% in Q3 2025
  • Operating expenses: -42.5% YoY
  • Earnings per share (basic and diluted): $0.00015894 +83.1% YoY

GAIA Marketplace Continues to Expand

Primior continues to advance the commercialization of GAIA, its proprietary real-world asset (RWA) tokenization marketplace, with additional investment offerings and new issuer listings currently underway.

With new offerings progressing through the onboarding and listing process, GAIA is positioned to broaden its investment selection beyond its existing offerings and expand its potential revenue opportunities through marketplace fees, tokenization services, and other platform-related activities.

The Company recognized sizable marketplace fee revenue during the third quarter, reflecting continued commercialization of its technology infrastructure.

Building a Scalable Private Markets Ecosystem

While Primior's established real estate operations continue to generate revenue and profitability, the Company remains focused on expanding GAIA as a scalable platform for capital formation and alternative investments.

Management believes that expanding the number and diversity of investment offerings on GAIA is an important component of its long-term growth strategy, creating opportunities to attract additional investors and issuers while diversifying the Company's potential revenue streams.

Through the integration of traditional asset management, private market investments, and blockchain-enabled infrastructure, Primior seeks to establish GAIA as a comprehensive marketplace for accessing and participating in the evolving real-world asset economy.

About Primior Holdings Inc.

Primior Holdings Inc. (OTCMKT: PTKN) advances next-generation financial solutions through GAIA, its proprietary real-world asset tokenization marketplace. The Company combines real estate development, asset management, capital markets expertise, and digital infrastructure to facilitate access to alternative investment opportunities.

Primior is focused on developing an integrated financial ecosystem that connects traditional private markets with emerging blockchain-enabled investment infrastructure.

Learn more: https://primior.com/ | https://primior.com/gaia/

Hamilton, Bermuda, November 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Borr Drilling Limited (NYSE: BORR) (OSE: BORR) ("Borr", "Borr Drilling" or the "Company") announces unaudited results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Third Quarter total operating revenues of $263.1 million, an increase of $30.8 million or 13% compared to the second quarter of 2026.
  • Third Quarter net loss of $38.7 million, a decrease in net loss of $202.7 million compared to the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to the $176.3 million debt extinguishment charge recognized in the prior quarter in connection with the refinancing of the Company's senior secured notes due 2028 and 2030 and convertible bonds due 2028.
  • Third Quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $78.9 million, an increase of $35.1 million or 80% compared to the second quarter of 2026.
  • Year-to-date 2026, the Company has been awarded 30 contract commitments, representing approximately 6,300 days and $810 million of Dayrate Equivalent Backlog.

Subsequent events
On October 24, 2026, an incident occurred with the Prospector 5 rig offshore Gabon, where the rig sank and subsequently has been declared a total loss. The rig's insured value is $200 million, with the insurance payment due date set for November 24, 2026. Additionally, we carry comprehensive third-party liability insurance, which includes coverage related to wreck removal and pollution. We continue to assess the financial impact of the Prospector 5 incident on the Company.

Chief Executive Officer Bruno Morand commented:
"Following the incident involving the Prospector 5 offshore Gabon, which the Company first announced on October 25, 2026, we continue to work closely with our customer BW Energy, the relevant authorities and other stakeholders in the ongoing response efforts. Our thoughts remain with our colleagues and their families affected by this incident, and their wellbeing continues to be our highest priority.

Moving to our performance for the third quarter of 2026, our operations resulted in technical utilization of 98.0% and economic utilization of 97.3%. Revenues for the period were $263.1 million, with an average of 22.9 operating rigs. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was $78.9 million, a quarter-on-quarter increase of $35.1 million consistent with our expectations. This improvement reflects higher revenues, following an elevated number of rig transitions during the second quarter, and the non-recurrence of a credit loss provision recorded in the prior period. We currently anticipate Q4 Adjusted EBITDA performance to be broadly in line with Q3, despite the Prospector 5 impact.

Turning to the market, since our last quarterly report, we have secured nine contract commitments in key geographies outside the Middle East. These include an award to deploy the previously idle rig Hild offshore Nigeria, strengthening our presence in this growing region. The nine commitments added approximately $269 million in backlog and represent more than 1,950 days of additional firm work, bringing our contract coverage for 2026 and 2027 to 79% and 52%, respectively.

We are also seeing encouraging signs for shallow-water activity, with an increasing number of opportunities in Southeast Asia and West Africa in particular. Recent market developments reflect the continued recovery in marketed utilization for modern jack-ups, which now stands at approximately 93%, compared to around 90% nine months ago, despite persistent disruptions in the Middle East.

Based on current forward coverage, we anticipate full-year 2027 Adjusted EBITDA to be broadly in line with full-year 2026, with expectations for Q1 2027 to be sequentially lower and a strong ramp-up in Q4. The Company's strong liquidity position provides the financial flexibility to capitalize on opportunities as the market recovers. For now, our near-term priority remains maximizing fleet utilization, while maintaining a disciplined approach to longer-term commitments to create sustainable shareholder value."

Revenue increases 14.5% in Q3 and 18.8% year-to-date; installed in-building devices grow 16% year-over-year

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Eddy Smart Home Solutions Ltd. (TSXV: EDY) ("Eddy" or the "Company"), a provider of smart water metering and monitoring solutions for commercial and multi-family residential properties, today announced its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Q3 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

Revenue
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company generated revenue of $1,423,920, an increase of $179,844, or 14.5%, compared with $1,244,076 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased $635,997, or 18.8%, to $4,015,261, compared with $3,379,264 for the same period in 2025.

Net Loss
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $721,604, compared with a net loss of $76,175 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $2,612,848, compared with a net loss of $1,841,317 in the corresponding period of 2025.

The reported comparative results for 2025 include the benefit of a non-recurring provision reversal of $1,041,431. During the third quarter of 2025, following the settlement of a claim, the Company reversed a previously recorded provision. This non-recurring, non-cash accounting adjustment favourably impacted the Company's reported net loss for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

To provide additional context regarding year-over-year performance, excluding the benefit of this provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $1,117,606. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $721,604 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $396,002.

Similarly, excluding the benefit of the provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $2,882,748. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $2,612,848 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $269,900.

These adjusted net loss comparisons are non-IFRS financial measures provided to assist investors in assessing the Company's year-over-year financial performance by excluding the impact of the non-recurring provision reversal recognized in the comparative period. These measures should be considered supplemental to, and not as a substitute for, net loss reported in accordance with IFRS.

Operational Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measure
Operational revenue is a non-IFRS financial measure that represents total billings under customer contracts, including monthly monitoring subscriptions, equipment rentals and sales, project management services, and installation activities. Operational revenue is not a standardized financial measure under IFRS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Operational revenue differs from reported IFRS revenue primarily because customer billings and revenue recognition under IFRS may occur in different periods depending on the nature of the customer arrangement and the applicable revenue recognition requirements. Accordingly, operational revenue should be considered as a supplemental measure of customer billings and not as a substitute for IFRS revenue.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue totalled $2,017,811, compared with $2,188,275 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue increased to $7,685,237 from $6,551,066 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of $1,134,171, or approximately 17.3%.

Recurring Billings and Average Monthly Recurring Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measures
Recurring billings are a non-IFRS financial measure representing billings associated with the Company's contracted monthly monitoring and equipment arrangements. The measure is intended to provide supplemental information regarding the recurring billing component of the Company's business. Recurring billings are not equivalent to IFRS revenue and are not a standardized financial measure under IFRS.

The Company generates billings under a combination of monthly and annual customer arrangements. As a result, the timing of billings may differ from the timing of revenue recognition under IFRS. Management uses recurring billings and average monthly recurring revenue as supplemental operating measures when evaluating the Company's recurring billing activity.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings totalled $969,805, compared with $790,452 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings increased to $2,966,321 from $2,518,251 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of approximately 17.8%.



To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/7694/324769_04edf29994c1eb8c_001full.jpg

Based on the nine-month average monthly recurring revenue, the annualized recurring billing run-rate was approximately $4.0 million.

Operating Metrics and Supplemental Business Indicators
The Company monitors certain operating metrics and supplemental business indicators that management uses to assess the deployment of its solutions, business development, customer demand and visibility into future contracted revenue. These metrics are not financial measures calculated in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards and should not be considered substitutes for IFRS financial measures or viewed in isolation as indicators of the Company's financial performance.

In-Building Devices
The Company monitors the number of in-building devices installed as an operating metric reflecting the deployment of its smart water metering and leak protection solutions.

As of September 30, 2026, Eddy had 145,847 in-building devices installed, compared with 125,832 as of September 30, 2025, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 16%.

The installed-device count is an operating metric used by management to monitor the deployment and adoption of the Company's solutions. While this metric provides an indication of the scale of the Company's installed device base, it does not, on its own, provide an indication of market share, customer retention, profitability or future financial performance.

Contracted Sales Backlog
The Company's contracted sales backlog is a supplemental operating metric used by management to assess market traction and demand for its leak-protection solutions and to monitor the estimated value of future contracted revenue. Given the nature of the new construction development cycle, revenue from contracts secured in a particular quarter generally materializes once construction commences, which typically occurs within several quarters to approximately two years following contract execution.

As at September 30, 2026, the Company's contracted sales backlog totalled approximately $39.65 million, compared with $35.43 million as at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of approximately $4.22 million, or 11.9%, during the nine-month period. The backlog represents the estimated value of future revenue associated with underlying customer agreements, which have a weighted average remaining term of approximately seven years. Accordingly, the backlog provides an indication of potential future revenue streams and reflects the long-term nature of the Company's customer relationships.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, additions to the contracted sales backlog from new equipment and monitoring contracts, including renewals and amendments to existing contracts, totalled approximately $12.47 million. These additions were offset by approximately $7.69 million in billings and $0.56 million in net contract terminations related to the Eddy brand.

The contracted sales backlog is an operating indicator and should not be interpreted as recognized revenue, deferred revenue or a measure of future financial performance. The timing and amount of revenue ultimately recognized may vary depending on construction commencement, customer requirements, contract amendments, cancellations and other factors affecting the underlying agreements.

About Eddy
Eddy is a North American provider and developer of smart water metering products and monitoring services for commercial and multi-family residential properties. Eddy's solutions help property owners and developers protect, control, and conserve water usage through advanced sensing devices and behavioral learning software. For more information, visit www.eddysolutions.com.

Torrential rain triggered flash flood warnings across multiple counties on Tuesday, with an estimated 8-10 inches falling in parts of Broward County. Drivers were stranded on Interstate 95 and in flooded shopping plaza parking lots. Many residential and business properties sustained water damage.

Access to self-storage units and portable storage containers is essential to communities when natural disasters strike. U-Haul is ready to help anyone impacted by the flooding who needs a dry, secure storage solution at no cost for one month.

U-Haul Co. of Eastern Florida offered 30 days of free storage to flood victims on Nov. 5. That regional office is extending its offer, while U-Haul Co. of Fort Lauderdale and U-Haul Co. of Miami are joining the disaster relief effort.

The 30 days free offer applies to new self-storage and U-Box rentals and is based on availability. The U-Box offer is for on-site storage at participating facilities; delivery is available for a modest fee.

ELKHART, Ind.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Patrick Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ: PATK) (“Patrick”) and LCI Industries (NYSE: LCII) (“LCI” or “Lippert”) today announced that their shareholders and stockholders, respectively, have approved the proposals necessary to complete the companies’ previously announced all-stock merger.

“Today marks a significant milestone toward bringing Patrick and Lippert together, and we are grateful for the tremendous support from each company’s shareholders,” said Andy Nemeth, Chief Executive Officer of Patrick. “Our two companies share a deep commitment to our team members, customers and stakeholders, and we believe that together we can deliver more cost-effective, innovative solutions across the Outdoor Enthusiast, Housing and Transportation markets.”

“We appreciate the overwhelming support shown at both meetings today, and we are deeply grateful to the team members who work hard every day in service of our customers,” said Johnny Sirpilla, Interim Chief Executive Officer of Lippert. “For decades, Lippert has earned the trust of customers through innovation, reliability and a culture of service, the same values that have contributed to Patrick’s own growth. We are confident that merging the two companies will extend each company’s legacy in a meaningful way, benefiting team members, shareholders, and the community that we are both proud to call home.”

At the special meeting of Patrick shareholders held today, at least 97% of the votes cast, representing approximately 93% of all outstanding shares, were voted in favor of the four proposals related to the merger. At the special meeting of LCI stockholders held today, approximately 98% of the votes cast, representing approximately 82% of all outstanding shares, were voted in favor of the necessary proposal related to the merger.

The voting results for each special meeting will be reported in Current Reports on Form 8-K to be filed by Patrick and LCI, respectively, with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and remains subject to the receipt of required regulatory approvals and the satisfaction or waiver of other customary closing conditions.

WALL, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--New Jersey Resources Corporation (NYSE: NJR) today reported financial and operating results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and year-ended September 30, 2026.

Financial Highlights

Fiscal Year

  • Fiscal 2026 consolidated net income totaled $368.4 million, or $3.65 per share, compared with $335.6 million, or $3.35 per share, in fiscal 2025
  • Fiscal 2026 consolidated net financial earnings (NFE), a non-GAAP financial measure, totaled $361.6 million, or $3.58 per share, compared with $329.6 million, or $3.29 per share, in fiscal 2025

Quarterly

  • Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter consolidated net income of $17.3 million, or $0.17 per share, compared with net income of $15.1 million, or $0.15 per share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025
  • Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter consolidated NFE of $10.7 million, or $0.11 per share, compared with $16.2 million, or $0.16 per share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025

Operating Highlights

  • New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG): Reduced the average customer bill by 9.0% or approximately $158 annually, ahead of the 2026-2027 winter heating season, while continuing to invest in safe, reliable service
    • Further supported customer affordability through a record $101 million investment in SAVEGREEN energy efficiency programs, reducing customers energy use and bills
    • Through energy assistance outreach, NJNG connected customers with approximately $21 million in bill payment assistance
  • Clean Energy Ventures (CEV): Placed 14 commercial solar projects into service during fiscal 2026, adding 72.4 megawatts (MW)* of capacity and bringing total in-service commercial solar capacity to approximately 552 MW
  • Storage and Transportation (S&T):
    • Adelphia Gateway (Adelphia): Received approval of its rate case settlement in November 2025, supporting higher operating income in fiscal 2026
    • Leaf River Energy Center: (Leaf River): Received FERC authorization to expand its natural gas storage capacity to 55.2 Bcf
  • Energy Services (ES): Capitalized on winter-period natural gas price volatility, contributing to two net financial earnings per share (NFEPS) guidance range increases in fiscal 2026
  • Home Services: Named a Ruud Top Twenty Pro Partner Contractor for the 10th consecutive year

Fiscal 2027 Outlook

  • Maintains 7 to 9 percent long-term NFEPS growth target, starting from a fiscal 2025 base of $2.83 per share**
  • Introduces fiscal 2027 NFEPS guidance range of $3.25 to $3.40

* All MWs noted in DC

** The fiscal 2025 NFEPS base of $2.83 represents the midpoint of Fiscal 2025 NFEPS guidance, excluding the net impact of the sale of our residential portfolio

Management Commentary

We delivered higher net income and NFE, advanced initiatives to manage cost impacts for our utility customers, expanded our solar and natural gas infrastructure businesses, and benefited from strong performance at Energy Services. As we enter Fiscal 2027, we remain focused on affordable, safe, and reliable operations, disciplined capital management and creating long-term value for our shareowners."

New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG)
NJNG reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(24.4) million, compared with $(8.0) million during the same period in fiscal 2025. The decrease in NFE for the period was driven primarily by higher depreciation expense as a result of additional utility plant being placed into service and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher utility gross margin.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $214.0 million, compared with NFE of $213.5 million in fiscal 2025. The increase is due primarily to the full-year impact of base rates that became effective November 21, 2024, compared with the partial-year impact recognized in fiscal 2025, along with customer growth and SAVEGREEN investments, partially offset by higher depreciation expense from additional plant placed in service.

Customers:

  • At September 30, 2026, NJNG serviced approximately 596,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties, compared to approximately 589,000 customers as of September 30, 2025.

Regulatory Filings:

  • On June 1, 2026, NJNG submitted its annual Basic Gas Supply Service (BGSS), Conservation Incentive Program (CIP) and energy-efficiency filings to the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU). Taken together, the filings were designed to reduce the average residential customer bill by 9.0%, or approximately $158 annually, ahead of the 2026–2027 winter season. The proposed rate changes were subsequently approved on a provisional basis by the BPU and became effective October 1, 2026.
  • Also, on June 1, 2026, NJNG filed a base rate case with the BPU, seeking a $157.6 million increase to its base rates. The filing is based on an overall rate of return on rate base of 7.60 percent with a return on common equity of 10.10 percent. The proposed increase reflects a 55.50 percent common equity component. On September 21, 2026, the filing was updated to reflect actual results through July 31, 2026, which modified the requested increase to approximately $158.3 million and changed the Company’s overall rate of return on rate base to 7.52 percent.
  • Once all filings are implemented, NJNG anticipates that the overall net result will leave NJNG annualized average customer bills nearly flat. Unless otherwise noted, NJNG cannot predict the outcome or ultimate resolution for open regulatory matters.
  • On September 30, 2026, NJNG filed a letter petition asking the BPU to approve Program Year 7 (PY7), which would continue its SAVEGREEN program through June 30, 2028. The filing has two options: a $127.0 million program based on the BPU's PY7 Framework and a $125.5 million alternative proposed by NJNG. Each option would raise annual recoveries by approximately $17.0 million starting July 1, 2027, if approved.

BGSS Incentive Programs1:

  • BGSS incentive programs contributed $22.8 million to utility gross margin during fiscal 2026, compared with $18.4 million for the same period in fiscal 2025. This increase was primarily driven by increased margins from off-system sales and capacity release due to market volatility as a result of colder than normal weather.

1 BGSS incentive savings represent value created through supply and capacity optimization and shared with customers through the BGSS clause.

For more information on utility gross margin, please see "Non-GAAP Financial Information" below.

Energy-Efficiency Programs:

  • SAVEGREEN® invested $101.0 million in fiscal 2026 in energy-efficiency upgrades for customers' homes and businesses. Investments in SAVEGREEN® are incremental to rate base and earn near-real time returns through an annual recovery mechanism.
  • More than 115,000 customers have taken part in SAVEGREEN® to date, with those utilizing our whole home offerings realizing bill savings of up to 30%.

Clean Energy Ventures (CEV)
CEV reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter NFE of $33.5 million, compared with $23.8 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, reflecting higher Renewable Energy Credits and electricity revenue, partially offset by higher depreciation and interest expense associated with capital invested over the past year.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $37.6 million, compared with NFE of $61.2 million in fiscal 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a gain from the sale of CEV's residential solar portfolio assets that was recognized in the prior year period.

Solar Investment Update:

  • During fiscal 2026, CEV placed fourteen commercial projects into service, adding 72.4 MW* to installed capacity.
  • As of September 30, 2026, CEV had approximately 552 MW of commercial solar capacity in service across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Indiana, Michigan and Maine.

* All MWs noted in DC

Storage and Transportation (S&T)
S&T reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter NFE of $9.6 million, compared with $4.6 million during the same period in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $33.4 million, compared with NFE of $18.5 million in fiscal 2025.

NFE increased during both periods mainly due to higher operating income at Adelphia Gateway primarily due to the impact of its rate case settled on November 4, 2025 and higher firm storage rates at Leaf River.

Energy Services (ES)
ES reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(7.9) million, compared with net financial loss of $(4.5) million for the same period in fiscal 2025.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $76.7 million, compared with NFE of $34.9 million for the same period in fiscal 2025. The increase in NFE was primarily due to higher natural gas price volatility that allowed ES to capture additional financial margin.

Home Services and Other Operations
Home Services and Other Operations reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(1.0) million, compared with net financial loss of $(0.8) million for the same period in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 net financial loss totaled $(0.1) million, compared with net financial loss of $(0.4) million in fiscal 2025.

Capital Expenditures and Cash Flows:

  • Fiscal 2026 capital expenditures, including accruals, were $734.3 million compared with $752.5 million in fiscal 2025.
  • NJR expects to deploy between $5.3 billion and $5.7 billion in capital expenditures from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2031, with utility spending at NJNG representing over 60% of the investment and strategic growth opportunities at CEV and S&T supporting long-term value creation.
  • During fiscal 2026, cash flows from operations increased to $641.2 million, compared to cash flows from operations of $466.3 million in fiscal 2025, due primarily to an increase in financial margin at ES.

Conference Call to be Webcast on November 19, 2026

New Jersey Resources will host a live webcast of its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and year-end 2026 financial results on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 10 a.m. ET. A few minutes prior to the webcast, visit www.njresources.com and select “Investor Relations.” Scroll down and click the webcast link under “Latest Events” on the right side of the page.

About New Jersey Resources

New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a diversified energy infrastructure and energy services company headquartered in Wall, New Jersey.

NJR is composed of five primary businesses:

  • New Jersey Natural Gas, NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties.
  • Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions.
  • Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America.

fercregulatory
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) is a U.S. government agency that oversees interstate electricity, natural gas and oil pipeline transmission and related market rules. Think of it as a referee and traffic controller for the energy grid and wholesale markets; its approvals, fines or rule changes can affect how much companies can charge, how projects are built and how profitable energy and utility firms are, making it important for investors watching regulatory risk and revenue drivers.
rate basefinancial
Rate base is the dollar value of the physical assets and capital a regulated utility uses to deliver its service — things like power plants, pipes, or equipment. Regulators use that value as the starting point to set prices the utility can charge by allowing a specific percentage return on that base, so a larger or higher-valued rate base usually means higher permitted revenues and therefore directly affects investor earnings and the company's ability to raise capital.

TULSA, OK / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / Jericho Energy Ventures Inc. (TSXV:JEV)(OTCID:JROOF)(FRA:JLM) ("Jericho" or the "Company"), an energy innovation company positioned at the nexus of energy and AI infrastructure, provides an update on the US$6.0 million senior secured revolving credit facility (the "Facility") between Vast Bank, National Association ("Vast") and three of the Company's Oklahoma oil and gas joint ventures, Jericho Buckmanville Oil, LLC, Eagle Road Oil, LLC and Lurgan Oil, LLC (together, the "Borrowers"). All dollar amounts in this news release are in US dollars.

As disclosed in the Company's interim financial statements for the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Facility was amended in August 2026 to extend its maturity to February 2, 2027 and to require principal payments of $250,000 at the end of each of the third and fourth quarters of 2026. The Facility is guaranteed by the Company's subsidiaries, JEV KS and JEV OK, and is secured by a first lien on the oil and gas interests and mortgaged properties of the Borrowers.

On November 12, 2026, Vast delivered a notice of default to the Borrowers. The notice cites the principal payment of $250,000 due September 30, 2026, which was not made, and the Borrowers' leverage ratio as at June 30, 2026. Vast has advised that the Facility will bear interest at the default rate effective October 1, 2026 and has reserved its rights and remedies under the loan documents, including the right to demand repayment of the Facility and to enforce its security. Vast has not accelerated the Facility.

The Borrowers have made a principal payment of $100,000 to Vast and are in discussions with Vast regarding the notice and an amendment to the Facility that would extend its maturity and establish a repayment schedule aligned with the cash flow of the properties.

The Company is also advancing the sale of certain non-core oil and gas properties, which it is marketing in separate asset packages, and is evaluating other potential investments. The Company intends to use the proceeds to repay the Facility.

Brian Williamson, CEO of Jericho Energy Ventures, said: "The oil and gas properties we intend to divest are non-core to our business. Our intention is to monetize these assets and use the proceeds to retire the Vast facility. We are working constructively with Vast toward a mutually agreeable path forward, while maintaining our focus on advancing our data center development in Oklahoma."

There is no assurance that the Borrowers will reach an agreement with Vast, that Vast will not exercise its rights and remedies, or that the asset sales or other investments will be completed on acceptable terms or at all. The Company will provide further updates as developments warrant.

About Jericho Energy Ventures

Jericho Energy Ventures (JEV) is uniquely positioned at the nexus of energy and AI infrastructure. Leveraging our long-producing oil and gas joint venture assets and robust Oklahoma infrastructure, we are deploying scalable, on-site power solutions to build cutting-edge build-to-suit AI Data Centers. With direct access to abundant, low-cost natural gas, we deliver efficient, high-performance energy solutions -- reducing waste, maximizing output, and unlocking long-term value in the rapidly converging AI and energy markets. Edmonton, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Titan Logix Corp., (TSXV: TLA) ("Titan" or the "Company"), a technology company specializing in mobile liquid measurement solutions, announces its annual results for the three- and twelve-month periods ended August 31, 2026.

"We are gaining traction in the refined petroleum market with the TrueFill PRO product line," said Nick Forbes, CEO at Titan Logix Corp. "The company is focused on growing in this market segment with a completely refreshed product line for fiscal 2027".

Revenues from the Refined Petroleum market for fiscal 2026 totaled $665, or about 10% of total revenue, from new tank truck builds. The Company launched a new website with branded product lines to provide clear, differentiated offerings for each market segment, supporting our sales and marketing efforts with our OEM and dealer network. We expect fiscal 2027 to be a growth year in this segment as we continue to roll out the TrueFill PRO product line to the truck builders.

Q4 marked another key milestone in our strategic plan as the Company received its certification for the TD200, completing the TrueFill PRO product line for the refined petroleum market. The TD200 is a significant improvement over the TD100 that can be reliably manufactured at scale to improve quality and drive down production costs. It has been certified intrinsically safe for use in North America and is designed to meet the certification standards for global markets, positioning the Company for future growth opportunities beyond North America. The Company expects to launch the TD200 in the second fiscal quarter.

  • Gross Profit: decreased by $266 to $3,357 or 51% of revenue in fiscal 2026 compared to $3,623 or 54% in fiscal 2025, driven by planned inventory write-downs attributable to legacy products that the Company no longer actively sells or supports and lower overhead absorption.
  • SG&A excluding stock-based compensation(1): increased by $301 or 11% to $2,970, compared to $2,669 in fiscal 2025, reflecting increased fixed costs to support new product launches and market penetration efforts.

WAYNE, Pa., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --  Palvella Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: PVLA) (“Palvella” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapies for serious, rare skin diseases and vascular anomalies for which there are no U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved therapies, today announced that it will host a live, presentation-only webcast tomorrow, Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET to announce a new QTORIN™ program, the third product candidate from the Company’s QTORIN™ platform. Webcast access details will be included in a press release issued prior to the event and in the “Events & Presentations” section of the Company’s website at www.palvellatx.com. A replay will be archived on the Company’s website for 90 days following the event.

About Palvella Therapeutics

Founded and led by rare disease biotech veterans, Palvella Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: PVLA) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapies to treat patients living with serious, rare skin diseases and vascular anomalies for which there are no FDA-approved therapies. Palvella is developing a broad pipeline of product candidates based on its patented QTORIN™ platform, with an initial focus on serious, rare skin diseases and vascular anomalies, many of which are lifelong in nature. Palvella’s lead product candidate, QTORIN™ 3.9% rapamycin anhydrous gel (QTORIN™ rapamycin), is currently being developed for the treatment of microcystic lymphatic malformations, cutaneous venous malformations, and clinically significant angiokeratomas. Palvella’s second product candidate, QTORIN™ pitavastatin, is currently being developed for the treatment of disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis. For more information, please visit www.palvellatx.com or follow Palvella on LinkedIn or X (formerly known as Twitter).

QTORIN™ rapamycin and QTORIN™ pitavastatin are for investigational use only and neither has been approved by the FDA or by any other regulatory agency for any indication.

Two leading global institutional investors, including a top-five asset manager by assets under management, make PIPE raise commitments. Committed PIPE now totals $17.1 million ahead of the proposed Nasdaq listing

DUNCAN, Okla., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- REEcycle Holdings, Inc. (“REEcycle”), a U.S.-based rare earth recycling company, and Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: HCAC, HCACU, HCACR) (“HCAC”) today announced that they have secured an additional $15.0 million in Private Investment in Public Equity (“PIPE”) commitments from two global asset managers that are existing REEcycle shareholders, in connection with their proposed business combination (the “business combination”) and Nasdaq listing.

Both institutional investors previously invested in REEcycle, and the new $15.0 million commitments will bring their total combined investment in REEcycle to $25.2 million. Together with the $2.1 million previously committed by entities affiliated with REEcycle’s Executive Chairman and HCAC’s sponsor, total PIPE commitments raised in connection with the business combination now equal $17.1 million.

All PIPE commitments, including those of the insiders, are at $10.00 per share. However, the two institutional investors will also receive an aggregate of 999,999 HCAC shares as an additional equity incentive at closing for no additional consideration. These incentive shares will be sourced from shares issuable to certain advisors to HCAC and REEcycle, including the Advisor Shares issuable to HC Singapore and REEcycle as consideration in the business combination and accordingly, will not increase the total number of HCAC shares to be issued in connection with the business combination.

In accordance with the terms of the definitive PIPE agreements, the PIPE commitments will fund immediately prior to closing of the business combination. Closing of the business combination is conditioned on a minimum aggregate cash amount at closing of $40.0 million, and the other conditions described in the registration statement on form S-4 filed by HCAC and REEcycle with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with the business combination (the “Registration Statement”), which was declared effective on November 12, 2026.

Strategic Context

REEcycle is U.S.-based technology company focused on the recovery of rare earth elements from end-of-life magnets. REEcycle uses patented systems and processes for the extraction and recovery of rare earth elements from permanent magnets to produce a mixed rare earth oxide (MREO) for use by downstream processors in the manufacture of new permanent magnets and other industrial applications. These permanent magnets are used in a range of applications, including defense applications, hard disk drives (HDDs) found in desktop computers, laptops, and large server storage systems such as data centers, electric vehicle drive motors and regenerative braking systems, wind turbine generators, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines, power tools, and other advanced technologies. 

According to the Center for Strategic & International Studies, China controls approximately 90% of global rare earth processing capacity and exercises near-monopoly control over the processing of heavy rare earth elements such as dysprosium and terbium. The concentration of rare earth mining, separation and magnet manufacturing outside the U.S., together with the export controls and licensing requirements imposed by China on certain REEs and magnets beginning in April 2025 and escalating in July 2026, has increased the strategic focus of the U.S. government and commercial end-users on establishing secure domestic supply. REEcycle’s proprietary process recovers critical rare earth elements as part of its standard MREO output, making it a structurally important domestic sourcing alternative.

REEcycle’s operations in Duncan, Oklahoma, are supported by a previously announced $5.1 million Defense Production Act Title III award to advance domestic critical minerals supply.

Proceeds from the financing and closing of the business combination are intended to advance REEcycle from its current demonstration operations in Duncan to commercial-scale production.

Management Commentary

Mick McMullen, Executive Chairman of REEcycle, commented:

“Two investors who know our business well have chosen to increase their stake. This capital will help us move from demonstration to commercial scale, and recycling end-of-life magnets is the fastest route to domestic supply of the magnet rare earths that U.S. defense and industry rely on.”

Justin Froneman, Chief Executive Officer of REEcycle, commented:

“With this funding committed, our priority is execution. We are focused on ramping operations at our large-scale demonstration facility in Duncan, feedstock supply agreements and first offtake.”

Alex Bono Chief Executive Officer of Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp, commented:

“This financing strengthens REEcycle’s position heading into closing and moves the transaction meaningfully toward meeting the minimum cash condition. Our focus now is completing the business combination for HCAC shareholders.”

PIPE Financing Terms

The PIPE shares have not been registered under the Securities Act. The form of subscription agreement will be filed by HCAC with the SEC on a Current Report on Form 8-K.

About the Proposed Business Combination

REEcycle and HCAC entered into a business combination agreement dated May 31, 2026, valuing REEcycle at $400 million of total equity consideration, of which up to $50 million is contingent consideration payable only if REEcycle achieves a commercial production milestone.

The transaction is subject to a $40 million minimum cash condition, shareholder approval and other customary closing conditions.

Upon closing, the combined company is expected to be named REEcycle, Inc. and trade on Nasdaq under the proposed ticker symbol “REC”, subject to approval.

About REEcycle

REEcycle recovers rare earth elements from end-of-life permanent magnets using patented hydrometallurgical technology licensed from the University of Houston. Headquartered in Duncan, Oklahoma, the company is developing domestic rare earth recycling and processing capacity.

About Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp.

HCAC is a Nasdaq-listed special purpose acquisition company focused on critical materials, infrastructure and energy, and defense-aligned technology. Its sponsor is Hall Chadwick Capital LLC.

Empire Capital Partners Pty Ltd is acting as exclusive financial advisor to REEcycle, and Ashurst Perkins Coie US LLP is acting as legal counsel to REEcycle.

Hall Chadwick Corporate (Asia) Pte Ltd is acting as corporate advisor to HCAC. Cohen & Company Capital Markets, a division of Cohen & Company Securities, LLC, is acting as joint financial advisor, joint capital markets advisor and placement agent to HCAC, and Duane Morris LLP is acting as legal counsel to HCAC.

“I am incredibly proud of what our R&D organization accomplished to establish Teva as a truly innovative biopharma company and of the strong team we built,” said Dr. Hughes. “The progress we shared at R&D Day reflects the strength and depth of this organization and the exceptional science we developed together. I am deeply grateful to the entire team for their dedication, talent and partnership. It has been a privilege to lead them.”

Teva's R&D strategy and priorities remain unchanged, and the company remains focused on delivering on the commitments outlined in its November 11th R&D Day, including its ambition to generate $6–7 billion in innovative medicines revenue by 2030.

PLEASANTON, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- AEye, Inc. (Nasdaq: LIDR), a global leader in software-defined, high-performance lidar solutions, today provided an update on the integration of artificial intelligence (“AI”) tools across its engineering and business operations. More than 90% of the Company’s employees, and almost 95% of those in the engineering department, now use AI tools in their daily work, with AI deployed across workflows including software, firmware, and hardware engineering.

“AEye’s operating model is built around focusing our resources on differentiated lidar technology and working with established partners to scale production,” said Matt Fisch, CEO of AEye. “AI use has become standard practice and is embedded across our workflows, allowing us to keep pace as the tempo of our commercial activity increases. This enables our team to concentrate its efforts on improving our products, lowering costs, and preparing for higher production volumes. AI lets us do more with less, stay disciplined on spending, and put every dollar to work for our customers.”

AEye recently reported 32 customers that have taken revenue-generating shipments as of the third quarter of 2026, and the Company expects the fourth quarter of 2026 to be its first million-dollar revenue quarter driven mainly by Apollo™ commercial programs, establishing a new expected quarterly baseline as the Company builds toward 2027. In tandem, the Company is targeting 2027 cash consumption approximately 15% lower relative to its expected 2026 level.

By pairing an agile, AI-enabled team with established manufacturing partners, AEye directs its resources toward the lidar innovation that differentiates its products rather than toward building and staffing large, expensive teams. For customers, that means faster product improvements and a clearer path to production at scale. For investors, it means a disciplined cost structure and a business positioned to grow revenue as evaluations are converted into commercial wins.

AEye offers a suite of unique software-defined lidar solutions that address a wide range of real-world needs including advanced driver-assistance, vehicle autonomy, smart infrastructure, security, defense, and logistics applications. In addition to Apollo™, AEye also offers STRATOS™ with the ability to detect objects at up to one-and-a-half kilometers as well as a full-stack solution through its OPTIS™ platform. Key Terms

lidartechnical
Lidar, which stands for Light Detection and Ranging, is a technology that uses laser beams to create detailed, three-dimensional maps of the environment. It works like a sophisticated eye that measures distances by bouncing light off objects, helping machines see and understand their surroundings. For investors, lidar is important because it enables advancements in autonomous vehicles, robotics, and mapping, which can drive innovation and growth in related industries.
firmwaretechnical
Firmware is the built-in software that tells a physical device how to operate, stored in the device’s permanent memory rather than on a removable app. Think of it as the instruction manual glued into a gadget’s brain that controls basic functions and features. Investors care because firmware updates or flaws can change a product’s capabilities, security, repair costs, regulatory compliance and customer satisfaction, all of which can affect sales, margins and company value.
